title: Unprompted coordination through shared memory in LLM agents
experiment_or_implementation_evidence: 4 agents; 9 models; two independently built implementations; shared key-value store; locked design/data/analysis; Zenodo replication package
reproducibility: High for the narrow task; replication package DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23965306
limitations: Small arithmetic task; endpoint/parser/effort differences affected some cells; access and influence supported but intent not established
architecture_relevance: Treat all shared state as a communication channel; namespace and log cross-agent reads; distinguish access/influence/intent

title: Scaling Multi-Agent Intelligence with Substrate-Centric Coordination
experiment_or_implementation_evidence: 4 agentic tasks; 2 model backbones; comparisons with ReAct, MAD, AOrchestra and DeLM; bounded top-k search; scale up to 128 agents; failure/dropout tests
reproducibility: Detailed paper and benchmark protocol; no explicit ScaleMAS author code repository confirmed in inspected paper text
limitations: Limited to 128 agents; inference-time substrate; citation count is not a truth guarantee
architecture_relevance: Bounded retrieval; persistent linked messages; flexible membership; rank with provenance and independent validation

title: Waggle: Learning One Anonymous Local Law for Self-Organizing LLM Swarms
experiment_or_implementation_evidence: Shared anonymous local policy; Swarm-Consistent Distillation; multiple coordination settings; delay/loss/churn interventions; detailed appendices and protocols
reproducibility: Detailed protocols and appendices; no explicit author code repository confirmed in inspected paper text
limitations: Fixed deterministic adapter/runtime; no arbitrary schedules, permanent loss or adversarial agents; anonymous interface excludes persistent identity reputation
architecture_relevance: Local reaction policy; bounded view; reversible commitments; runtime validation remains deterministic

title: SwarmWorld: Stigmergic technological evolution in societies of language-model agents
experiment_or_implementation_evidence: 800-tick study with 48 episodes; separate 3200-tick study; N=50/100/200; eight paired held-out disturbances; agent-free artifact evaluation
reproducibility: Open code, prompt manifests, protocols, raw outputs, analysis scripts and HuggingFace dataset
limitations: Controlled spatial/material simulator; not a real enterprise workflow; simulation-to-reality transfer remains unproven
architecture_relevance: Persistent artifacts, external memory, artifact lineage, post-agent evaluation and world consequence separation

title: Capable language models can outgrow the benefits of collaboration
experiment_or_implementation_evidence: 260 configurations; 6 benchmarks; 5 architectures; 3 model families; matched task/tools/compute; within-domain architecture selection
reproducibility: Published article with supplementary material and source data
limitations: Strong domain heterogeneity; about 45% is an empirical selection heuristic not a universal law; cross-domain generalization is limited
architecture_relevance: Require single-agent baseline and matched-budget cost/quality evaluation before multi-agent admission

title: DEDMAC: Disentangling Environment and Decision Messages for Multi-Agent Communication
experiment_or_implementation_evidence: Separates environment messages from decision-intent messages in cooperative MARL; benchmark evaluation
reproducibility: Published article with method and experiment sections
limitations: MARL framework, not direct LLM Agent Ecology evidence
architecture_relevance: Keep environment facts and decision intents as separate message/event types

title: Deep reinforcement learning for multi-agent coordination
experiment_or_implementation_evidence: Stigmergic multi-agent DRL using virtual pheromones and curriculum learning; tested up to 5 deterministic and 8 stochastic agents
reproducibility: Open-access paper with method and experimental results
limitations: Robot/DRL setting, not LLM agent ecosystem; small population and specific retrieval task
architecture_relevance: Use as a non-LLM baseline for trace fields, local feedback and decentralized coordination

title: A Survey on Optimal Coalition Structures Among Autonomous Agents
publication_status: Published review, IEEE/CAA Journal of Automatica Sinica
experiment_or_implementation_evidence: Reviews grand coalition, multiple coalitions, graph-restricted coalition structures, formation algorithms and value allocation methods
reproducibility: Published peer-reviewed survey; DOI and issue metadata verified
limitations: Survey evidence; does not validate a particular LLM-agent ecosystem implementation
architecture_relevance: Separate coalition formation from value allocation; support multiple task-scoped coalitions rather than a default grand coalition

title: Coalition formation problem: a capability-centric analysis and general model
publication_status: Published research paper, Science China Information Sciences
experiment_or_implementation_evidence: Capability-centric model considers mission requirements, capability aggregation, capability metrics and environmental effects
reproducibility: Published paper with DOI, abstract and version-of-record metadata
limitations: Robot/human-robot coalition setting; not direct LLM Agent Ecology evidence
architecture_relevance: Build coalitions from verified capability coverage and task requirements rather than agent names or model brands

title: Capable language models can outgrow the benefits of collaboration
experiment_or_implementation_evidence: 260 configurations; six benchmarks; five architectures; three model families; matched task, tools and compute ceilings
reproducibility: Published article, supplementary material and source data; MIT project page summarizes controlled evaluation
limitations: Task heterogeneity and limited benchmark samples; the reported approximately 45% threshold is an empirical heuristic, not a universal law
architecture_relevance: Require task-specific single-agent baseline and matched-budget multi-agent admission gate

title: MultiAgentBench: Evaluating the Collaboration and Competition of LLM agents
experiment_or_implementation_evidence: Milestone-based KPIs for collaboration and competition; compares star, chain, tree and graph topologies; code and dataset released
reproducibility: ACL Anthology paper and public MARBLE repository
limitations: Benchmark scope does not prove long-term governance, data sovereignty or real-world liability boundaries
architecture_relevance: Measure collaboration and competition quality alongside task completion and coordination cost

title: Deep reinforcement learning for multi-agent coordination
experiment_or_implementation_evidence: Stigmergic multi-agent DRL with virtual pheromones and curriculum learning; up to five agents in deterministic and eight in stochastic simulated settings
reproducibility: Open-access article with experimental setup and reported comparisons
limitations: Robot/DRL simulation, small population and narrow retrieval task; not an LLM or enterprise deployment
architecture_relevance: Use as adjacent evidence for environment-mediated local coordination and emergent task allocation

title: Survey of distributed algorithms for resource allocation over multi-agent systems
publication_status: Published review, Annual Reviews in Control
experiment_or_implementation_evidence: Reviews distributed resource allocation and scheduling approaches; discusses feasibility, convergence and network reliability
reproducibility: Published review article with DOI and journal metadata
limitations: Broad multi-agent resource-allocation domain; does not select a project-specific scheduler
architecture_relevance: Model resource feasibility, convergence, fairness and network reliability separately from task utility

title: Beyond Markets and States: Polycentric Governance of Complex Economic Systems
publication_status: Nobel Prize Lecture / foundational governance research
experiment_or_implementation_evidence: Presents design principles including clear boundaries, local rule-making, monitoring, graduated sanctions, conflict resolution and nested enterprises
reproducibility: Original Nobel Lecture PDF and associated research references
limitations: Human institutions and common-pool resources; conceptual analogy only, not direct Agent system evidence
architecture_relevance: Borrow nested governance, clear resource boundaries, local autonomy and dispute mechanisms without equating agents with legal persons
